title: feat(objectql)!: sync-in provenance columns on synced objects, stamped by the pull and refused elsewhere
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBEaJzgBWzjWCNjBjkVoeRto)_

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzeX8NmUPt5KSzQar4X

Part of #32062

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none (no skills/ page names the `_sync_` columns or the synced bucket's injected columns; grep of `skills/**` for `_sync_`, `managedBy: 'synced'` and `SYNC_PROVENANCE` finds nothing)

## 维护者速读

Slice 5 of the sync-in P2 engine, route A of the seat's revised order: the D4 column half. Every `managedBy: 'synced'` object now gets five hidden, read-only `_sync_` columns and an index on (`organization_id`, `_sync_source`, `_sync_external_id`). Both pulls stamp four of them on every row they write. Any other write that names a `_sync_` column is refused with `400 ERR_SYNC_PROVENANCE_WRITE_REFUSED`, system context included. That refusal is the narrowing. `_sync_deleted_at` is planned but nothing stamps it until slice 6 (D3). No authorable key changes.

## What changes

- **Plan (spec).** `resolveInjectedSystemColumns` gains `plan.sync`, true for `managedBy: 'synced'` only (and false under `systemFields: false`, like every other column). It adds `SYNC_PROVENANCE_COLUMNS` to `names`. `injectedSystemColumnDefs` / `SYNC_PROVENANCE_FIELD_DEFS` hold the five definitions (`hidden`, `readonly`, `system`, not required). New exports: `SYNC_PROVENANCE_COLUMNS`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_PREFIX`, `SyncProvenanceColumn`, `SYNC_PROVENANCE_FIELD_DEFS`. `ERR_SYNC_PROVENANCE_WRITE_REFUSED` joins the error-code ledger under `@objectstack/objectql`.
- **Registry (objectql).** `applySystemFields` injects the five columns from the plan, and `provisionSyncProvenanceIndex` appends the index after the tenant index (led by `organization_id` when the object has it). The write-side inverse (`stripProvisionedSyncProvenanceIndexFrom`) runs before the tenant inverse in `stripMaterializedStampsFrom`, so the tenant stamp stays last for its own re-stamp-and-compare. `materializeBaseLayer` provisions it the same way.
- **Write refusal (objectql).** `refuseSyncProvenanceWrite` runs in `insert` and `update` right after `assertWriteAllowed`, before middleware, defaults and hooks. It refuses any payload key starting `_sync_` unless the context carries `SYNC_PULL_WRITE` (a `Symbol.for` key, same shape as `SUMMARY_RECOMPUTE_WRITE`). The engine consumes the mark, so a hook's `ctx.api` write inside the pull's write is refused like any other system write. After the `before*` hooks are sealed, `refuseHookSyncProvenanceWrite` compares each row's `_sync_` keys with the snapshot taken before the hooks. A key a hook assigned, changed or removed is refused (`by: 'hook'`) before the driver, on any write, the pull's own included.
- **Pulls (service-automation).** Both pulls stamp `_sync_source` (the mapping name), `_sync_external_id`, `_sync_pulled_at` and `_sync_run_id` through `stampSyncProvenance`, after the mapping projects the rows and before `runImport`. They write with `markSyncPullWrite(context ?? { isSystem: true })`. A mapping whose `fieldMapping` targets a `_sync_` column is refused `400 mapping_target_refused` before any read or write. Before this PR it was already refused as an unknown target. A connector pull whose target definition cannot be read is refused the same way before the call, as the datasource pull already did.
- **Diagnostics (metadata-protocol).** `computeMetadataDiagnostics` drops the injected `_sync_` columns from a served object before the parse. They have to be exactly the platform definitions; an author `_sync_` field is still refused for the reserved prefix.
- **Docs.** The `jobs.mdx` bullet "Every row says where it came from", one sentence on the `synced` row of `objects.mdx`, notes on the liveness rows `mapping.deletePolicy` and `object.managedBy`, and regenerated references.

## Decision for review: composite `upsertKey` encoding (ADR-0153 open question L853)

`encodeSyncExternalId` (`packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-provenance-stamp.ts`, which cites the open point):

- **One key field:** its value as plain text. A string is trimmed, as the runner matches it. A number, bigint or boolean goes through `String()`, a date through ISO 8601, anything else through JSON.
- **Several fields:** `JSON.stringify` of the array of those spellings, in the order `upsertKey` declares them, never sorted. So `upsertKey: ['amount','external_no']` gives `["10","A-1"]`. The order is the author's declaration, so it stays stable for as long as the mapping does. JSON escaping keeps a value that contains `","` unambiguous.
- **Any blank key value:** no id is stamped. The runner skips that row anyway (a blank match key).
- Within one mapping the number of key fields is fixed, so the plain spelling and the array spelling never meet among rows of one `_sync_source`.

This changes nothing an author may declare; the stamp only reads `upsertKey`. Pinned in `sync-provenance-stamp.test.ts` and in `datasource-pull.test.ts` (the composite case).

## `_sync_deleted_at`: planned, unstamped

The column is in the plan and injected, and no gate trips on it. Its description says nothing writes it until delete marking lands, and the `mapping.deletePolicy` liveness row (still `planned`) says the same. Slice 6 (D3 + N1–N5) stamps and clears it.

## Acceptance notes

- **Two mappings on one target (L854):** not refused. Each row carries its `_sync_source`, so slice 6 can scope its mark by it.
- **`_sync_run_id` without a run ledger:** not written. The import runner reads a blank cell as "leave the field as it is", so `null` could not clear it either. On a row such a pull created, the column is empty. On a row it updated, it keeps the earlier id. The column description says this. That composition already logs a warning once at boot.
- **`systemFields: false` on a synced target:** no columns, so its rows are written unstamped, as before. Refusing it would narrow what an author may declare, which this slice does not take; D3, which needs the columns, can judge it.
- **What the refusal judges:** the caller's payload before anything runs, and the hooks' writes to the `_sync_` keys before the driver.
- **`_sync_external_id` for a transformed key:** taken from the mapped value the row is matched on, before a `lookup` resolves. The column description now says so.

## Narrowing

The engine refuses a `_sync_` key in any insert or update but the pull's, `isSystem` included (ADR-0153 D4: "A `_sync_` column in any write except the pull's is refused by name, whatever the caller's context"). Before this PR no object carried such a column (`ObjectSchema` reserves the prefix), so such a write was naming a column that did not exist. A `before*` hook that writes a `_sync_` key is refused the same way, and on the pull's write too.

## Deviations from the claimed surface

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/metadata-diagnostics.ts` (+ its test): without it, every served synced object reads `valid: false` for the reserved `_sync_` prefix once the columns are injected.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts`, `engine-update.ts`, `index.ts`, `registry-object-registration.ts`, `sync-provenance-*.ts`: these are the claimed "objectql system-field consumer" and "the door that refuses `_sync_` writes", named file by file.
- `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts` (the new wire code's ledger row, ADR-0112) and `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts` (the definitions the plan rows inject).
- `content/docs/data-modeling/objects.mdx`, `automation/hooks.mdx`, `automation/flows.mdx`: one sentence each; `packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`: the reader-ledger row for the new index.
- `packages/core` is untouched.

## Verification

- Full package suites on the merged tree: objectql 636/636 files, service-automation 294/294 files; spec (880 files) and metadata-protocol (366 passed, 9 skipped) green before the main merge. Targeted and typecheck green for all four packages.
- Ablations, each on disk, then restored: with the caller-payload refusal disabled, 3 cases in `sync-provenance.test.ts` go red; with the hook-write refusal disabled, 4 go red.
- `dispatch-gates --ran`: 128 derived families accounted for. 125 ran green. 3 are NOT-MEASURED because a local prerequisite is missing (exit 3): `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needs a deeper clone, and `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` need a full build.
- Dogfood battery on `805d6199`: os-verify-lock VERDICT command-exit 0; Test Files 487 passed, 3 skipped (490); Tests 4125 passed, 68 skipped. It is re-run on the rework head, and the result is in the report.
- Fix round for L1 7119029164 / contract review 7119012685:
  - S1: the hooks' `_sync_` writes are judged, with tests for a hook on a system write and on the pull's write (insert and update).
  - S2: a connector pull with an unreadable target is refused, with a test.
  - N2: the description is aligned.
  - N7: this section and the open-point line are corrected.
